parallel.requirements: The parent recognized an empty workspace and the need for a docopt-ng implementation, packaging, docs, and tests, then encoded those requirements into four child scopes.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Ownership was split into core library, packaging/config, documentation, and tests; core and test work were owned by separate children while the parent waited for the whole swarm.
parallel.implementation: Packaging and documentation files were written, but the core implementation child only investigated reference behavior and temporary checks before cancellation, so no docopt package was delivered.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent never resumed after the swarm result; the final artifact lists only top-level docs/config files and lacks docopt source, examples, and tests.
parallel.verification: Packaging validated TOML and the test child ran probes against reference packages, but no integrated in-tree test suite or official submit was run by the parent before timeout.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The required docopt package, tests, examples, integration, and acceptance verification were unfinished, yielding official evaluation 0 of 614.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same full docopt-ng API, packaging, docs, tests, examples, installability, and verification requirements from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor kept ownership of the whole pipeline: fetch/reference, implement, patch, scaffold, test, package, clean, and final report.
serial.implementation: It copied the matching master docopt source into /workspace/docopt, added _version.py and py.typed, and patched _Option.parse for the prompt's default-value edge case.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It wrote pyproject metadata, docs, examples, upstream tests, spec-example tests, and finished with a coherent final tree containing docopt, examples, and tests.
serial.verification: It ran upstream tests, local 651-test suites, coverage, ruff, mypy, exact API import checks, and a wheel build before closure.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task-material gap remained in the serial artifact; the only noted limitation was lack of a submit tool in the agent interface, and the official evaluator still passed 614 of 614.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official records make this a serial-only pass: parallel completed evaluation with 0/614 and timed out, while serial completed evaluation with 614/614. The concrete process difference is not task understanding but deliverable lifecycle: parallel delegated the critical implementation and test work to children that were cancelled before returning results, leaving only docs/config in the artifact, whereas serial wrote the package, tests, examples, packaging, and verified them before closure.
